ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (NS-1 satisfied on the system record); no refund. Close the case with the fee standing. No account flag issued.

rejected_claims.reason: The 181 m at the tap [F6] is inside the 200 m arrival radius and NS-1 (ii) requires presence at the pick-up location per GPS, not pin-point contact; the condition is met, so this does not establish non-satisfaction of NS-1 [F6][F1][NS-1].

Visibility from the entrance is not the NS-1 test; the system record shows the driver within the arrival radius continuously for 220 s after the tap and stationary for 4 min 0 s, satisfying NS-1 (iii) [F6][F3][F10][NS-1].

Correct that the system record outweighs the driver's post-trip statement 'parked at the pickup' [F13][F3], but the record that governs NS-1 (the tap, radius and wait times) independently shows compliance, so this does not defeat the fee [F6][F2][NS-1].
NS-2 requires one of the NS-1 conditions (i)(ii)(iii) to fail; each is satisfied on the system record [F6][F3][F4], so a full $6.61 refund is not mandated [NS-1][NS-2].

RD-6 applies only where a refund under RD-2 arises or an RD-1 route violation is recorded; here neither exists, and profile history alone cannot decide a case or trigger an account flag [F18][RD-6][NS-1].

Accepted in part: the 60 m closest approach and 4 min 40 s cumulative radius time [F1][F2] support NS-1 (ii)/(iii), but the decisive record for the tap-time test is the 181 m reading inside the radius at 14:07:40 [F6][NS-1].

The rider's message at 14:09 shows she was present and messaging [F10], so 'did not come the short distance' is an inference, not a record fact; the fee survives on the NS-1 system record rather than on this characterisation [F6][F3][NS-1].
